Return crowd photos (>= min_faces detected faces) grouped by time gaps.
min_faces defaults to the live config.FACE_CROWD_MIN_SIZE setting.
start_ts/end_ts is the People page's time Focus.

post.description:
Ignore all unlabeled faces in the given crowd photos. ``undo``: see
/api/faces/undo.

get.description:
Download a compact JSON backup of the user-authored data (places,
people/families, face labels, settings) — see backup_service for exactly
what's included/excluded and why.

post.description:
Re-attach a backup (the JSON /api/data/backup downloads, as the raw request
body) to the current library. dry_run defaults to TRUE so a stray call changes
nothing: it returns the same report the real run would. Additive only;
conflicting values are skipped unless overwrite=true. See
backup_service.restore_backup.

get.description:
Download history (dataset_downloads table) — a future update-check
feature's raw material: url, size, record count, and when, per download.

get.summary: Api Data Face Model Download Status
Api Data Semantic Model Download Status

get.description:
Which raw GeoFabrik extracts are still cached — the street search only works
while they are, since nothing about streets is ingested into a database.

List faces, one page at a time: ``offset``/``limit`` slice a stable
ordering (every scope's sort ends in a face-id tiebreaker), and the response's
``total`` / ``next_offset`` (null on the last page) tell the People grid how
much is left to "Load more".

scope=unlabeled attaches a recognition suggestion to each face;
scope=suggested returns only unlabeled faces whose *best* guess is `person_id`,
ranked by confidence — for quickly approving one person's guesses in bulk.
suggested_only (scope=unlabeled) drops faces with no guess, scanning up to the
suggest cap so it finds matches beyond the first detection-ranked page.

start_ts/end_ts (epoch secs) are the People page's time Focus. They window the
candidate faces for the unlabeled and suggested scopes only (person/all/recent/
ignored ignore them, and the recognition gallery stays global either way).

post.description:
Assign (person_id / name) or unassign (clear=true) faces; exactly one of
the three. ``assigned`` is the number of faces that exist and were written
(including faces already on that person); ``not_found`` counts ids matching
no face. 404 if none of the ids exist, 400 on empty ``face_ids``.

Current state of an explicit set of faces, as face_item dicts (no
suggestion), plus the ids that no longer exist. The People page calls it on
load to re-validate staged decisions restored from sessionStorage (U7):
a face deleted (nuked, rescanned) since is dropped, one already in its
staged state is dropped, one changed elsewhere is flagged. POST because the
id list can run to thousands — too long for a query string.

get.description:
Discover groups of likely same-person faces among the unlabeled queue, so a
new person can be named in one go (no seed example needed). Clusters the top
`cap` faces by detection score (they cluster cleanest); the rest are reachable
afterward via per-person 'Find more'. ``full`` returns every face item per
group (not just a 24-face sample) — total stays bounded by the cluster cap.
threshold/min_size/cap default to the live config.FACE_CLUSTER_* settings.

post.description:
Move faces to the come-back queue: people we know or suspect but aren't
ready to assign yet. Distinct from /ignore (that's for strangers/false
detections we never want to see again). come_back=false restores faces to
the unlabeled queue. ``undo``: see /api/faces/undo.

get.description:
Representative-led review groups for one person: each stored
representative face, paired with up to `group_limit` other labeled faces
(same person) ranked closest-to-representative first. Based on the stored
representative flags, not a fresh re-cluster — run Recompute first if a
person doesn't show up in /api/faces/dedup/persons yet.

People who currently have representative-flagged faces (from the last
recompute) — the picker for the Representative Faces review page.

post.description:
Recompute representative-face flags for every person with enough
labeled faces (see the Representative faces settings group). Safe to
re-run any time — e.g. after tagging more photos, retagging, or tuning
the threshold/fraction settings; always recomputed from scratch.

Hide faces from the unlabeled queue (background strangers, false detections),
or restore them with ignored=false. ``undo``: see /api/faces/undo.

Mark faces as 'definitely not person_id' (negative=true), or lift that
(negative=false). Removes person_id from these faces' recognition ranking so
they stop being suggested as this person and fall through to their next-best
match. Distinct from /ignore, which hides a face from every queue.

Nuclear option: hard-delete every face (detected, assigned, or ignored) for
the given photos and wipe every cached rendition (thumbnail, preview, face
crops) so a rescan starts completely from scratch. Irreversible.

Nuke + re-detect in one call: wipe every face and cached rendition for the
given photos, then run detection over them again. Manual assignments for these
photos are lost (same as /nuke) — this is the "detection went wrong, start
over" action, not a routine incremental scan.

Detect faces for up to `limit` not-yet-scanned photos. Repeat until
`remaining` is 0. 503 (detail {code, message, errors}) when the batch aborted
without marking anything — the model failed, or too many files in a row were
unreadable — and the client must stop rather than walk on (audit F1).

Put every photo whose file couldn't be read back in the detection queue.
Those photos were never marked scanned and have no detected faces, so the
rescan can't touch any tag.

get.description:
Face-pipeline counts for the People nav. The Focus (start_ts/end_ts time
window) scopes only unlabeled_faces (the one windowed nav scope);
total/ignored/tagged stay global to match the un-windowed
All/Ignored/Recently-tagged scopes.

post.description:
Revert one face/person write: hand back the ``undo`` token its reply
carried (assign, ignore, come-back, crowds/ignore-unlabeled, DELETE person).
Each face goes back to its exact prior state unless it changed since —
those come back in ``conflicts`` and are left alone. A deleted person is
re-created first (same id when still free; ``person_id`` either way); 409
if their name has been taken meanwhile, with nothing written.

delete.description:
Delete a hand-drawn face (undo for a mis-drawn box). Detected faces are not
deletable — 400 — because the next scan would re-detect them; use ignore.

post.description:
Assign (person_id / name) or unassign (clear=true) one face; exactly one
of the three, else 400. 404 for an unknown face or person.

get.description:
Square crop of one face. Same failure mapping and caching as the photo
renditions (api/_media.py): 404 unknown face or vanished file, 422 undecodable.

post.description:
Reverse-geocode up to `limit` photos that have coordinates but no location.
Repeat until `remaining` is 0. Returns 503 if no geocoding dataset (OSM, Census
or GeoNames) is installed.

get.description:
US Census place polygons overlapping a viewport bbox, as a GeoJSON
FeatureCollection — backs the Places DB map's census overlay. These are the
boundaries consulted after OSM and before the GeoNames distance estimate, so
seeing them explains why an unincorporated coordinate resolves the way it does.
503 if the census places DB hasn't been built.

post.description:
Write up to `limit` geotagged photos' GPS coordinates (plus resolved place
names, where available) into their XMP sidecars — only photos whose sidecar
doesn't already hold their current values. Client loop: pass `after_id` =
the previous response's `cursor` and repeat until `remaining` is 0. Returns
{processed, written, failed, errors_sample, cursor, remaining}. A bodyless
POST runs one default-sized batch from the start.

get.description:
Reverse-geocode a single coordinate exactly as a photo taken there would be —
returns the {city, sublocation, postal_code, state, county, country, country_code}
that would be persisted on that photo, plus each source's own answer under
`sources` (OSM containment, Census place containment, ZCTA/ZIP containment,
GeoNames nearest-point). Backs the Places
DB map's click-to-probe: click a point and see what location the geocoder would
save, and why. 503 only if none of the datasets is installed.

OSM place polygons overlapping a viewport bbox, as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection
— backs the Places DB map's OSM boundary overlay (cities, parks, stadiums,
campuses, neighborhoods, named buildings), rendered via Leaflet's L.geoJSON().
`buildings=false` excludes the building category (the map only asks for it
past its own building-level zoom threshold — see MIN_ZOOM_FOR_BUILDINGS).
503 if the OSM places DB hasn't been built. `total`/`truncated` are extra
top-level fields alongside the standard `type`/`features` — GeoJSON consumers
that only look at `features` are unaffected.

GeoNames places within a viewport bbox — backs the Places DB map, which
plots the raw reverse-geocode reference data (not photos) so the user can
verify what place names a coordinate would resolve to.

Boundary cells for GeoNames places in a viewport bbox — for each place, the
area a coordinate must fall in to reverse-geocode to it. Exact Voronoi cells
under the plain nearest-point lookup; grid-traced outlines (accurate to about
one grid step of the viewport) when the population weighting is on, since those
boundaries are curved — see geocode.voronoi_cells. Backs the Places DB map's
cell overlay, shown once zoomed in far enough.

ZIP code areas overlapping a viewport bbox, as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection —
backs the Places DB map's ZIP overlay. Each feature carries the ZIP plus its
crosswalk city, i.e. the mailing city a photo inside it can fall back to.
503 if the census DB hasn't been built, or was built without the ZCTA layer.

Recurring drop points mined from the coordinates already on the photos.
Clustered so drops a few hundred feet apart at the same real place count as
one entry, and (by default) with the ones a saved place already covers left
out.

The four bounds narrow the answer to a patch of the world — what the Custom
Places page sends to ask "what's in view here that I never named?". Give all
four or none.

Feeds the geocode page's location picker (the "Hotspots" section of
Tag as… dialog in frontend/src/pages/geocode/) and the Custom Places page's hotspot
list — the places you tag at repeatedly but never bothered to save a name
for. See services/hotspots_service.py.

geotagged neighbors. POST because a selection can be hundreds of ids.

Revert a commit: hand back the `previous` snapshots from the /api/geotag,

get.description: Return a guessed lat/lng from nearby-in-time geotagged photos (±window seconds).

List persons. With a start_ts/end_ts window (the People page's time Focus),
people with no faces in range are omitted.

face_count is opt-in (``face_counts=true``, the Manage page): the hot callers
(People page, tag pickers) don't need it and index.get_persons dropped the
count for latency. When requested it is each person's *total* assigned faces
— exactly what DELETE /api/persons/{id} would unlabel — regardless of any
time window.

Delete a person; their faces become unlabeled. ``undo`` is the token
POST /api/faces/undo takes to bring them back (same id, attributes, faces).

patch.description:
Update a person's name, birth/not-before/not-after dates, and/or family.
Only fields present in the request body are changed — send just the fields
you want to update.

post.description:
Merge person ``person_id`` into ``req.into``: every face, representative
flag and "not this person" negative moves to the target, empty target
attributes are filled from the source, and the source is deleted — all in
one transaction (see index.merge_persons for the per-table rules). Returns a
summary of what moved.

get.description:
On-the-fly full-resolution render with detected face boxes drawn on, as JPEG.

Powers the detail pane's "View full size" button for RAW files: decodes the RAW

draws each face's box + name, so the new tab shows the real pixels — not the
downscaled preview. Heavy (full decode + draw), so it runs in the executor and is not
disk-cached; boxes reflect current labels, so it must not be cached either.

post.description:
Bundle the selected photos' original files (full quality, RAW included
as-is) into a ZIP archive for download.

The archive is built into a temp file and sent with a Content-Length — never
held in memory. Selections with no existing files are 404, selections over
GEOTAGGER_ZIP_MAX_BYTES are 413. ``?check=1`` runs just that validation and
returns the counts, so the page can surface an error before it commits to a
navigation download (which would otherwise replace the page with the error
JSON). Files missing from an otherwise valid selection are skipped; their
count is reported (``skipped`` / ``X-Skipped-Files``).
Revert exactly the batch a prior /api/photos/commit-guessed-dates call made.

Set photo timestamps to absolute targets (the Time Sync save). Idempotent:
re-sending the same body after a partial failure only applies what's left.
Same {results, written, failed, not_found} reply and status rules as
/api/geotag, plus 409 when every refusal was a conflict (the photos' dates
changed since the client loaded them).

Add a hand-drawn face box to a photo, optionally already assigned to a
person. For faces detection missed entirely. ``bbox`` is normalized 0..1 in
display space (as drawn over the oriented preview); the server maps it to
sensor space and tries to embed it so the face still joins recognition.

On-the-fly full-resolution render with detected face boxes drawn on, as JPEG.

Powers the detail pane's "View full size" button for RAW files: decodes the RAW
at full resolution via LibRaw (see thumbnails.render_fullsize_with_faces) and
draws each face's box + name, so the new tab shows the real pixels — not the
downscaled preview. Heavy (full decode + draw), so it runs in the executor and is not
disk-cached; boxes reflect current labels, so it must not be cached either.

People already committed to a face in this photo, one entry per face.

Deliberately lighter than /api/photos/{photo_id}/faces: no embeddings and no

`stats` is opt-in because it costs a spatial query per place: the Custom

Forget recorded failures so the next scan retries every one of them,
including unchanged files it would otherwise skip. Refused during a scan,
whose snapshot of the table would make the result confusing.

get.description:
Files the scan could not index (persisted across runs, newest failure
first) plus every warning of the most recent run (in memory only — the
console prints just a sample). One small indexed read; not polled.

Background startup-scan progress. A separate route (not a field on
/api/status) because the nav banner polls it every ~2s and /api/status runs a
COUNT(*) on the photos table; this one is pure in-memory state.

Search photos by any combination of date range, location, people, camera,
folder, GPS accuracy, and whether a face was detected. All supplied criteria
combine with AND; person_mode controls whether multiple people must appear in
the *same* photo ('all') or any one of them does ('any').

With `text` (or `similar_to`), the other filters pick the candidate set and the
semantic model ranks it: results below the score threshold are dropped and each
photo carries a `score`.

Paged: `offset`/`limit` slice a stable ordering. `total` is the true match
count, `truncated` says this page holds fewer than all of them, `next_offset`
(null on the last page) is where "Load more" continues, and `histogram` buckets
the whole result set for the timeline. `ids_only=true` returns
{ids, datetimes, total} for every match instead (Select all across pages).

One-shot health snapshot for the home dashboard: library size, geotagging /
reverse-geocoding / face-labeling progress, and people counts.

Distinct years with a dated photo, newest first — the People page's Year
Focus dropdown used to get this by fetching /api/stats/months and picking out
the years, which forced a strftime()-per-row + GROUP BY over the whole photos
table just to throw away the month/geotag breakdown. Instead, walk year
boundaries via idx_photos_datetime: each year is a single indexed
"does a row exist in [start, end)" range-seek that stops at the first match.

Component health. A component being unavailable (ExifTool missing, no
GeoNames data) is a normal, reportable state: 200 with that component's
``available: false`` + ``reason``. The DB is not optional — without it
nothing works — so a failing COUNT is a 503, never a 200 whose ``db_total``
is an error string (audit A12: that made `res.ok` lie).
